summary.title: Lab 3 - Threat Model of the GOSAJEC LTD Hostel WLAN
summary.description: STRIDE threat model of a student hostel WLAN (open SSID with captive-portal login, Starlink uplink, Ruijie switch and 8 APs). Course CY 475.

data.name: TB1: Wireless medium / client zone (untrusted)
data.description: Radio space where students, visitors and attackers can all transmit and listen.

data.name: TB2: Hostel network (managed infrastructure)
data.description: APs, switch, portal, management plane and data stores operated by GOSAJEC LTD.

data.name: TB3: Internet edge
data.description: Boundary between the hostel network and the public Internet via Starlink.

data.name: E1 Resident Student
data.description: Registered student using a laptop or phone (maximum two devices per account).

data.name: E2 Non-resident User
data.description: Friend or visitor who gains access only through shared credentials or a resident's hotspot.

data.name: E3 Attacker
data.description: Malicious resident or external person within radio range of the hostel.

data.name: P1 Ruijie Access Points (8)
data.description: Eight Ruijie APs (4 per block) broadcasting the GOSAJEC LTD SSID, associating clients and forwarding frames.

threats.title: Evil twin / rogue AP impersonating GOSAJEC LTD
threats.description: An attacker broadcasts the same SSID with a stronger signal so devices auto-join it, then relays or alters traffic and shows a fake login page. Enabling weakness: Open SSID with no AP authentication or server certificate; devices reconnect to any network with a known name.
threats.mitigation: Use 802.1X with server-certificate validation (EAP-PEAP/TTLS or EAP-TLS) so clients can verify the network; enable Ruijie rogue-AP/WIDS detection; run periodic RF walk-throughs.

threats.title: ARP spoofing and man-in-the-middle between students
threats.description: A malicious resident poisons ARP caches on the shared subnet to intercept or modify other students' traffic, or scans and attacks neighbouring devices. Enabling weakness: No client (peer-to-peer) isolation on the APs and no dynamic ARP inspection; students share one broadcast domain (A3, A4).
threats.mitigation: Enable AP client isolation; turn on DHCP snooping, DAI and IP source guard on the Ruijie switch; place each block or floor in its own VLAN; rely on HTTPS end to end.

threats.title: Capture and cracking of hidden WPA2/WPA3 SSID handshakes
threats.description: Hidden SSIDs seen in the scan are revealed by standard tools, then a captured WPA2 handshake is cracked offline if the passphrase is weak. Enabling weakness: Hiding an SSID gives no real protection; WPA2/WPA3 transition mode permits WPA2 downgrade; passphrase strength unknown (A9).
threats.mitigation: Remove unused SSIDs; for any remaining PSK network use a random passphrase of 16 or more characters or WPA3-SAE only; put staff or management SSIDs on a separate VLAN.

data.name: P2 Captive Portal and Authentication
data.description: Web login that checks each student's credentials and applies the two-device limit (assumed A1).

threats.title: Captive portal phishing and cloned login page
threats.description: Behind a rogue AP or through DNS manipulation, the attacker serves a copy of the hostel login portal and harvests usernames (Gmail addresses) and passwords. Enabling weakness: Users are conditioned to type credentials into a web page after joining; no mutual authentication between portal and user (A1, A2).
threats.mitigation: Serve the portal only over HTTPS with a CA-signed certificate on a fixed, published domain; enable HSTS; teach students to check the address; move to 802.1X so no password is typed into a web page.

threats.title: Weak, default or reused student passwords; brute force on the portal
threats.description: An attacker guesses passwords for accounts created with predictable initial passwords, or replays leaked Gmail passwords (credential stuffing) at the portal. Enabling weakness: Accounts are provisioned by the operator; no evidence of forced password change, complexity rules, lockout or MFA (A10).
threats.mitigation: Force a password change at first login; set minimum length and complexity; throttle and lock out repeated failures; screen against breached-password lists; advise students never to reuse their Gmail password.

data.name: P3 Ruijie Switch / Gateway
data.description: Ruijie switch (and gateway functions) providing DHCP, DNS, NAT, routing and the Starlink uplink.

threats.title: DNS spoofing and redirection
threats.description: Forged DNS replies send students to malicious sites or a fake portal. Enabling weakness: Plain-text, unauthenticated DNS; clients can use any resolver; no DNSSEC validation (A5).
threats.mitigation: Force clients to use the gateway resolver, with DNS-over-TLS upstream and DNSSEC validation; block outbound DNS to other resolvers; combine with DAI.

threats.title: Physical tampering, theft or unauthorised wired access
threats.description: Someone unplugs, resets or steals an AP or the switch, or plugs a laptop into an exposed Ethernet port to bypass the portal. Enabling weakness: Equipment in shared hostel areas; unused ports not disabled; no port security (A8).
threats.mitigation: Mount APs out of reach; lock the switch and Starlink router in a ventilated cabinet; disable unused ports, enable port security, apply tamper seals and keep an asset register.

threats.title: Exploitation of unpatched firmware
threats.description: A known vulnerability in outdated AP, switch or gateway firmware is exploited to take control of a device or pivot into the management network. Enabling weakness: No documented patch management for the Ruijie devices; firmware versions unknown (A7).
threats.mitigation: Keep a firmware inventory; apply vendor updates after testing; subscribe to Ruijie security advisories; schedule quarterly reviews.

data.name: P4 Management Interface
data.description: Local web interface or cloud console used to configure the switch, gateway and APs.

threats.title: Default or weak administrator credentials
threats.description: An attacker or curious student logs into the AP, switch or gateway admin page with vendor-default or guessed credentials and reconfigures the network. Enabling weakness: Default or shared admin passwords; management pages reachable from the student network (A6, A7).
threats.mitigation: Change all default credentials; use unique, long passphrases kept in a password manager; create separate named admin accounts; enable lockout; restrict management to a management VLAN.

data.name: E4 Network Administrator
data.description: Person who creates student accounts and manages the equipment.

data.name: D1 Student Account Database
data.description: Usernames (Gmail addresses), passwords and account status.

threats.title: Breach of the student account database
threats.description: Theft or leak of the account store exposes student Gmail addresses and password data, enabling credential stuffing against other services. Enabling weakness: Storage protection (hashing, encryption) unknown; broad admin access; backups possibly unprotected (A10).
threats.mitigation: Store passwords salted and hashed (bcrypt or Argon2); encrypt the database and backups; limit access; collect minimum data and comply with the Data Protection Act, 2012 (Act 843).

data.name: D2 Session and Device Table
data.description: Active sessions, MAC/IP bindings and the per-account device count.

threats.title: Bypass of the two-device limit
threats.description: A student changes or randomises MAC addresses, or places a router/hotspot behind one device, to connect more than two devices per account. Enabling weakness: The device count is presumably tracked by MAC address, which is easily changed or randomised (A5).
threats.mitigation: Enforce the limit on authenticated sessions per account rather than MAC address; adopt 802.1X identities; alert when many MACs appear for one account.

data.name: D3 Configuration and Logs
data.description: Device configurations, administrator credentials, backups and event logs.

threats.title: Tampering with logs and exposure of configuration backups
threats.description: An intruder deletes or edits logs to hide activity, or reads exported configuration backups that contain passwords and keys. Enabling weakness: Logs stored only on the device; configuration backups possibly unencrypted (A8).
threats.mitigation: Send logs to a remote server the devices cannot modify; encrypt and access-control configuration backups; monitor file integrity.

data.name: E5 Internet (Starlink)
data.description: External networks and services reached through the Starlink terminal.

data.name: F1 Wi-Fi association and data
data.description: Student device joins the open SSID and exchanges all data frames with the AP.

threats.title: Passive sniffing of unencrypted Wi-Fi traffic
threats.description: A resident or visitor in radio range captures frames from the open SSID with a monitor-mode adapter and reads unencrypted traffic (HTTP pages, DNS queries, cookies, app metadata). Enabling weakness: SSID is advertised as open ([NONE]/[OPEN]); there is no 802.11 encryption, so every frame is readable over the air.
threats.mitigation: Replace the open SSID with WPA2/WPA3-Enterprise (802.1X) using the existing student accounts via RADIUS; as an interim step enable Wi-Fi Enhanced Open (OWE). Enforce HTTPS and advise a VPN on public networks.

threats.title: RF interference and co-channel congestion
threats.description: Several APs and neighbouring networks share 2.4 GHz channel 1, causing contention and drops, whether accidental or deliberate jamming. Enabling weakness: Overlapping 2.4 GHz channel plan (two GOSAJEC LTD BSSIDs observed on channel 1) and unavoidable neighbouring networks.
threats.mitigation: Plan channels (1, 6, 11 on 2.4 GHz), lower transmit power, steer capable clients to 5 GHz, use Ruijie auto-RF tuning and repeat site surveys.

data.name: F2 Portal login
data.description: Username and password submitted to the captive portal through the AP.

threats.title: Credentials intercepted on the way to the portal
threats.description: If the login form or redirect uses HTTP, or students click through certificate warnings, credentials cross the open air interface in readable form. Enabling weakness: Unencrypted wireless medium plus a possible HTTP portal or invalid certificate (A2, to be verified).
threats.mitigation: Make the portal HTTPS-only (TLS 1.2 or higher) with a valid certificate, disable the HTTP login page, and never put credentials in URLs.

data.name: F3 Shared-credential access
data.description: Non-resident connects using a resident's credentials or hotspot.

threats.title: Credential sharing and hotspot relaying to non-residents
threats.description: A resident gives a friend their login or tethers a hotspot, so unauthorised people use the bandwidth and their actions are attributed to the resident. Enabling weakness: Knowledge-only authentication; the two-device limit does not stop sharing within the limit or tethering.
threats.mitigation: Publish an acceptable-use policy with sanctions; alert on simultaneous logins from different APs or blocks; offer time-limited visitor vouchers on a rate-limited guest SSID to remove the incentive to share.

data.name: F4 Rogue AP / deauth / sniffing
data.description: Attacker traffic towards the wireless medium: rogue beacons, deauthentication frames, sniffing.

threats.title: Deauthentication / disassociation flooding
threats.description: An attacker sends spoofed deauthentication frames to disconnect students, disrupt study sessions or push devices onto a rogue AP. Enabling weakness: Management frames are unprotected; 802.11w (PMF) cannot be enforced on an open network.
threats.mitigation: Require 802.11w (PMF), available with WPA3, OWE and WPA2/3-Enterprise; enable WIDS alerts for deauthentication floods.

data.name: F5 Wired trunk (Ethernet/PoE)
data.description: Student traffic carried from the APs to the Ruijie switch.

threats.title: Rogue DHCP server or DHCP starvation
threats.description: A device on the LAN answers DHCP requests with a malicious gateway or DNS, or exhausts the address pool so new clients cannot connect. Enabling weakness: DHCP snooping and rate limiting not enabled; flat Layer 2 network (A4, A5).
threats.mitigation: Enable DHCP snooping with only the uplink port trusted; rate-limit DHCP; use port security and storm control.

data.name: F6 Redirect and auth check
data.description: Unauthenticated clients are redirected to the portal; authentication result returned to the gateway.

data.name: F7 Account lookup
data.description: Credential verification against the stored student accounts.

threats.title: Insider misuse of account administration
threats.description: A staff member creates, alters or shares accounts without authorisation, or accounts of departed students stay active and are resold. Enabling weakness: No role separation or audit of account creation; no account lifecycle management.
threats.mitigation: Use role-based administration; log account creation and changes; audit accounts each semester and disable them at the end of residence.

data.name: F8 Session binding
data.description: Authenticated MAC/IP recorded; device count checked.

threats.title: Session hijacking by cloning an authenticated MAC/IP
threats.description: After a victim logs in, the attacker copies the victim's MAC and IP while the victim is idle and uses the authenticated session without credentials. Enabling weakness: Authenticated clients are whitelisted by MAC/IP; weak session binding and long timeouts (A5).
threats.mitigation: Bind sessions to MAC, IP and port with dynamic ARP inspection and IP source guard; shorten idle timeouts; use client isolation.

data.name: F9 Internet traffic (Starlink)
data.description: All student traffic to and from the Internet over the single Starlink link.

threats.title: Bandwidth exhaustion of the shared Starlink link
threats.description: Heavy downloads, torrents, 4K streaming or a deliberate flood by a few users saturates the single uplink and degrades service for everyone. Enabling weakness: No per-user rate limiting or fair-usage QoS is evident; satellite capacity is limited and shared (A8).
threats.mitigation: Apply per-user and per-device bandwidth limits and fair-usage QoS; restrict P2P and bulk traffic at peak hours; monitor Starlink usage and set alerts.

threats.title: Single uplink failure (outage, obstruction, power loss)
threats.description: Dish obstruction, weather, terminal fault or a power cut takes the whole hostel offline because everything depends on one Starlink connection. Enabling weakness: Single Internet path and single point of failure; failover link and UPS not mentioned (A8).
threats.mitigation: Add a secondary uplink (4G/5G or another ISP) with automatic failover; protect the dish, router and core switch with UPS and surge protection; monitor link health.

data.name: F10 Admin login
data.description: Administrator authenticates to the management interface.

threats.title: Compromise of the management account or cloud console
threats.description: Phishing or password reuse gives an attacker the administrator's login, allowing changes to SSIDs, accounts and policies on all eight APs. Enabling weakness: Single-factor admin authentication; no least-privilege roles; management plane not separated from user traffic (A6).
threats.mitigation: Enable MFA on the management/cloud account; apply least-privilege roles; alert on admin logins; allow management only from a management VLAN or VPN.

data.name: F11 Read/write config
data.description: Configuration, credentials and backups read and written.

data.name: F12 Config push
data.description: Configuration pushed to the switch, gateway and APs.

threats.title: Insecure management protocols
threats.description: Administrator credentials and configuration travel over HTTP, Telnet or SNMPv1/v2c and are sniffed by a student on the same network. Enabling weakness: Legacy management services enabled by default; management traffic not segregated (A6).
threats.mitigation: Disable Telnet, HTTP and SNMPv1/v2c; use SSH, HTTPS and SNMPv3; restrict management with ACLs on a management VLAN.

data.name: F13 Event logging
data.description: Gateway and switch write events to the log store.

threats.title: Insufficient logging and loss of accountability
threats.description: A student abuses the network (illegal downloads, attacks) and denies it; with shared credentials and no retained logs, the operator cannot show who did what. Enabling weakness: Authentication, session and NAT logs may not be retained or forwarded; clocks may be unsynchronised; accounts are shared (A8).
threats.mitigation: Forward gateway, switch and AP logs to a central syslog server; record login, MAC, IP and timestamps; synchronise time with NTP; set a retention policy aligned with the law.
